scene.metaphor: A miniature data-labeling workbench where useless repeats are filtered out before a few high-value specimens reach the annotator.
scene.setting: A polished studio tabletop built like a tiny industrial sorting line: cool-gray felt surface, matte metal rails, a shallow mesh sieve, and a clean receiving tray with cobalt and mint accents and one restrained warm coral note on Tal’s clothing.
scene.frozen_incident: Tal is mid-sort with tweezers, calmly nudging a clump of identical paper tokens through a mesh filter while one stubborn duplicate is caught halfway and a single unique token has just rolled toward the label tray.
physical_materials: paper tokens cut into simple rounded rectangles and speech-bubble shapes
one small coral fabric accent on Tal's top
semantic_anchors: Tal as a recognizable smiling operator
scene.image_instruction: Create a serious studio photograph of Tal as a recognizable operator on a miniature labeling workbench. Use his dark curly hair, salt-and-pepper beard, and warm focused smile; place him left-of-center, leaning into the set with tweezers in hand, wearing a simple top with one restrained coral accent against an otherwise cool-gray scene. In front of him, a tiny practical conveyor line on brushed metal rails feeds a dense pile of identical gray paper tokens into a mesh sieve, where repeated pieces are being removed before only a few cobalt and mint tokens reach a clean tray. Freeze a harmless absurd moment: one duplicate is stuck half-through the sieve while a single useful token has just slid free. Keep the composition lateral and low for a 3:1 banner, with generous negative space on the right, one dominant subject, and no more than three large supporting props. Polished lighting, crisp tonal separation, tactile handmade materials, and a miniature-world realism should make the joke readable even at thumbnail size.
